briefing.headline: The simulation predicts the mandate would roughly triple departures over the next 12 months, from about 472 to about 1,468 of 5,000 employees (about 1,000 extra leavers, +222%), with sentiment strongly negative (-1.48 on a -2 to +2 scale).
briefing.most_at_risk: Caregivers (+282%), mid-level staff and managers (+266%), and long commuters (+259%) react worst because fixed days, long drives and VP-only exceptions collide with family duties and feel like distrust, while juniors with short commutes react least (+172%) and some see office visibility as a career boost.
risks: You lose experienced mid-level people and managers, the hardest to replace. Voices with 10 to 15 years' tenure say they are already job-hunting, and managers predict their teams are too.

The policy hits women (+248% vs +209% for men) and caregivers hardest, which could create visible diversity and fairness problems. It also opens the company to scrutiny over how exceptions are granted.

Badge tracking and VP sign-off are read as 'they don't trust us,' which damages engagement even among people who stay. Because competitors still offer flexibility, people actively looking have somewhere to go.
design_changes: Let teams pick their own anchor days instead of company-set days, so people can plan around school runs and caregiving.
Drop individual badge-swipe reviews with managers, or limit them to aggregate office-use reporting. The surveillance element drives resentment even among short-commute staff with no caring duties.

Move exception approval to direct managers, with published criteria for caregivers and very long commutes (roughly 60+ minutes each way), and extend the 90-day runway or phase in from two days to three.
briefing.confidence: medium. The direction is consistent across every group and every sample voice, but the size of the increase rests on only 48 modelled voices, and many people who say they are 'looking' never actually leave. Treat the tripling as a warning sign, not a forecast.

subgroup_checks.claim: Bigger rise for mid and senior managers
